package: W52-01 — bounded wait for a live worktree store lock
question: Do concurrent worktree operations have to fail when the store lock is held by a live process?
answer: No. A live owner is awaited for a bounded, abort-aware period (default 30 s); a dead owner is still reclaimed immediately and the ownership verification is unchanged.

sourcePosition.evidence: dead-owner policy from W47-02 (_x/Rze/P1t/zPo in chunk-sfn1dbxq.js; Iue/Nm in chunk-3sda67c1.js); the wait itself is a local store decision.

behavior.loop: O_EXCL acquire; on EEXIST reclaim a dead owner and retry, otherwise wait 50 ms; abort ends the wait; deadline fails closed
behavior.unchanged: reason format, size bound, dev/ino release check, dead-owner reclaim

changes.change: lockWaitMs option, abortable pause, bounded acquisition loop
wait/abort case and fail-fast lockWaitMs 0 in the two fail-closed tests
three C-4 rows record the completed lock contention work
worktree relocation row records the bounded wait

tests.added: a live store lock is awaited until the owner releases it

residuals: A holder that runs longer than lockWaitMs still causes the waiter to fail closed.
There is no queue fairness; waiters race and the first successful open wins.
The wait deadline is per operation, not a global scheduler.
